title: Container vs VM: What's the Difference?

scenes.say: Containers and virtual machines sound similar. But how are they really different?
A virtual machine runs its own operating system and kernel on a hypervisor. A container shares the host's kernel and uses a container runtime.

scenes.label: Speed
scenes.sub: VMs: minutes to boot. Containers: seconds.
scenes.say: VMs can take minutes to start. Containers launch in seconds.

scenes.label: Resources
scenes.say: VMs are heavy, often gigabytes in size. Containers are much lighter, usually just megabytes.
Choose VMs for strong isolation or legacy apps. Use containers to package and scale modern apps.

scenes.question: Do containers run their own kernel?
scenes.wrong: Yes, each has its own kernel.
scenes.right: No, containers share the host's kernel using namespaces and cgroups.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Do containers run their own kernel? No—they share the host's kernel and isolate processes with namespaces and cgroups.
